summary: Establishes the explicit Year One digital product team and shared capability needed to deliver King’s Edge, support the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release and learn what enduring digital product capability King’s requires.
detailSummary:
Digital Innovation and Product Development Capability establishes the team and working practices through which King’s Edge and the first Digital Student Experience Hub release are delivered. During 2026/27, the capability itself is part of the discovery: King’s tests how much core capacity is needed, which specialist inputs must be reliably available, and which product and operating practices are required for sustainable delivery.

The Year One funded core is 4.0 FTE across four explicit posts. The Senior Backend & Integration Engineer (1.0 FTE) owns backend services, domain/API integration, technical integration with King’s systems and senior engineering judgement. The Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer (1.0 FTE) provides hands-on delivery across the student-facing Hub and King’s Edge experience and supporting application services. The UX/UI Designer (1.0 FTE) provides full-time interaction and interface design across the shared Hub and Edge journeys. The QA Engineer (1.0 FTE) owns test strategy, automated and manual quality assurance, regression and release quality, with a potentially later start once code production is established. The current holding cost for these four posts is £201,000 for approximately November 2026 to June 2027; Digital and IT must replace this with grade- and start-date-based costing before the business case is finalised.

The four funded posts are not the whole delivery capability. For planning transparency, the current working hypothesis is that Year One also requires approximately 2.5 FTE-equivalent of existing or shared capacity over the periods in which each function is active: 0.3 FTE Product Owner, 0.5 FTE delivery coordination/agile facilitation, 0.5 FTE service design, 0.5 FTE business analysis, 0.2 FTE user research, 0.2 FTE DevOps/platform support, 0.2 FTE pooled technical and assurance input and 0.1 FTE live-service/support collaboration. A further 0.2 FTE solution-architecture allocation is required only if the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer cannot credibly carry that function. These are working deployment assumptions for James Costerton and Digital and IT to validate; they are not additional funded posts in the current business case.

Mark Peace remains the direct Product Owner during mobilisation. The substantive build demand remains King’s Edge, with the same team establishing the reusable Hub foundations and focused first-release experience under 4.1.2. Broad Year One Hub discovery therefore has protected service-design, business-analysis and user-research capacity rather than expecting the four funded posts to absorb discovery alongside build. Security, privacy, accessibility, data and live-service specialists are drawn in at the points the work requires them.

The delivery model should test agentic software-development tooling as an accelerator for experienced engineers, but no incremental agentic-tooling cost is included in the baseline Year One funding ask until Digital and IT confirms whether existing capacity can be shared and what any additional instance would actually cost. The existing KAI team is not assumed to transfer wholesale into the capability, but reusable technical assets, including Azure AI Foundry components, should be assessed and adopted where they fit the target architecture.

By the end of Year One, King’s should have both delivered product capability and evidence about the capability model itself. Actual throughput, quality, discovery demand, integration effort, specialist dependencies, tooling productivity and live-service obligations should determine the team shape and investment required in Years Two and Three.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s does not currently have a sufficiently dependable multidisciplinary product capability for turning emerging student-experience needs into working, supported digital services at pace. Requirements can be addressed through conventional system change, local initiatives, temporary projects or standalone products, making prioritisation and reuse difficult.

King’s now needs enough in-house capability to deliver a substantial King’s Edge roadmap and establish the first Digital Student Experience Hub foundations, while also supporting broader discovery of the student digital estate. The precise enduring team shape is not yet known well enough to justify fixing it in advance.
caseForChange.opportunity:
An explicit four-post funded product core, combined with named shared discovery, delivery and specialist capacity, gives King’s a disciplined route from need to supported change without pretending that four people alone can carry the whole programme. One transparent capability model can connect prioritisation, research, service design, product design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and learning.

King’s Edge supplies the first substantive product demand. The Digital Student Experience Hub extends that work into reusable shared foundations and a focused institutional release, while broad discovery informs the next phase.
caseForChange.whyNow:
King’s Edge creates an immediate requirement for dependable in-house digital product delivery. At the same time, the Digital Student Experience Hub needs a focused September 2027 first release and a wider evidence base for the remainder of the mobilisation.

2026/27 is therefore the right point to mobilise the four funded posts, explicitly protect the shared capacity they depend on, test agentic development where useful and learn through real delivery. Future expansion should follow evidence about throughput, journey demand, integration complexity, quality and operational load.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s has a dependable multidisciplinary digital product capability with a transparent pipeline, clear decision rights and repeatable practices for discovery, design, engineering, quality, assurance, release and continuous improvement.

During 2026/27, the funded 4.0 FTE core delivers the King’s Edge replatform and agreed product roadmap and supports the focused first Digital Student Experience Hub release. Approximately 2.5 FTE-equivalent of named shared capacity supports product ownership, delivery coordination, service design, business analysis, user research, DevOps/platform work, assurance and live-service collaboration, with up to 0.2 FTE additional solution architecture if the senior engineering role cannot absorb it. Digital and IT must validate these deployment assumptions before mobilisation.

The capability can then expand or change shape where live demand and evidence justify it, with future staffing, tooling and recurrent costs confirmed through the wider three-year mobilisation business case rather than carried forward as automatic assumptions.

benefits.title: King’s responds more quickly to emerging student needs
benefits.statement: Priority needs can be translated into tested digital responses in shorter cycles, with student and staff evidence shaping development before large commitments are made.
benefits.realisationPeriod: From establishment of the first delivery pipeline
benefits.successLooksLike: Priority needs move predictably from discovery to evaluated live use, and users can influence solutions while they remain adaptable.

benefits.title: Digital delivery becomes more predictable and evidence-led
benefits.statement: A transparent pipeline, explicit capacity decisions and consistent product and assurance practices make needs, priorities, progress and trade-offs clearer.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.realisationPeriod: As the operating model becomes routine
benefits.successLooksLike: Demand is prioritised through one route, delivery commitments are visible and changes in team capacity can be explained by actual roadmap evidence.

benefits.title: Successful innovation becomes sustainable institutional provision
benefits.statement: Valuable changes have a defined route into secure, supported and appropriately owned operation, while multidisciplinary capability remains available for continuous improvement.
benefits.beneficiary: Students, service owners, Digital and IT and King’s
benefits.successLooksLike: Successful capabilities have explicit ownership and support arrangements, unsuccessful trials close cleanly, and the product capability has an evidence-based route into business as usual.

steps.title: Recruit and mobilise the core multidisciplinary digital product team
steps.summary: From September through November 2026, secure funding and recruit or assign four explicit Year One posts through Digital and IT: 1.0 FTE Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, 1.0 FTE Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, 1.0 FTE UX/UI Designer and 1.0 FTE QA Engineer. In parallel, validate and name the approximately 2.5 FTE-equivalent shared capacity required across Product Ownership, delivery coordination, service design, business analysis, user research, DevOps/platform support, assurance and live-service support, plus up to 0.2 FTE solution architecture if not covered by the senior engineering post.

steps.title: Establish the product operating model and delivery practices
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish one transparent pipeline, prioritisation and capacity cadence, proportionate discovery and user involvement, engineering and quality expectations, agentic-development practices where useful, embedded assurance and release practices across King’s Edge and the Digital Student Experience Hub.

steps.title: Prove the capability through King’s Edge, broad discovery and the focused Hub release
steps.summary: From January to October 2027, prove that the funded core and named shared-capacity model can deliver the substantive King’s Edge roadmap and focused Digital Student Experience Hub release while protected discovery capacity maps the wider estate and priority journeys. Use evidence to identify real capacity gaps before expanding the team.

steps.title: Make product operations and live-service collaboration routine
steps.summary: From November 2027 to February 2028, make operating practices routine across the live Digital Student Experience Hub and King’s Edge product domain, balancing roadmap delivery, incidents, maintenance, quality, discovery and continuous improvement.

steps.title: Scale the team and its practices where the wider roadmap justifies it
steps.summary: From March to October 2028, expand or reshape the core and specialist capability only where live-service evidence, broad discovery and the confirmed wider student-journey roadmap justify additional throughput or expertise.

steps.title: Embed an enduring institutional product-development capability
steps.summary: By the end of the three-year mobilisation, establish the sustainable multidisciplinary capability, professional leadership, governance, product practices and interfaces with SED product ownership and Digital and IT specialist/platform services. Confirm recurrent staffing, tooling and costs from live evidence before business-as-usual transition.
